source.publication: Instructions for 2025 PIT-ADJ; 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions
source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 1 ('If an item is not listed, it is not a valid New Mexico addition, exemption, or deduction'); Form PIT-B line 3 and its NOTE; PIT-1 instructions PDF page 28, line 20 NOTE; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = NM government pension (person 0) 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 32,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 50,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 17,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 50,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (single) row for federal AGI 50,000.00 gives 0.00 x 1 qualifying = 0.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 0.00. Line 17 = 50,000.00 + 0.00 - 17,750.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 32,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 32,250.00 = 32,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 32,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 15,750.00 = 677.25; total 1,111.75, to the cent 1,111.75. The table row over 32,200 to 32,300 gives 1,112; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,111.75. A New Mexico government pension has no line on PIT-ADJ, so it stays in income.
